title: Spike a typed provider registry covering one provider's launch contract
description:
Objective: find out whether provider launch policy can be centralized before anyone commits to moving 11,000 lines of Bash and PowerShell. The roadmap calls a typed provider registry the enabling refactor, and also warns against a wholesale launcher rewrite before a vertical slice proves the contract.

Deliverable: a written decision plus a typed registry definition covering one provider only. Add a provider descriptor type naming argv and config construction, session mode, event capabilities, resume support, terminal handoff and failure classification, populate it for a single provider, and add contract tests asserting the descriptor reproduces the argv and config that scripts/moe-agent.sh and scripts/moe-agent.ps1 build for that provider today. Record the findings in docs/plans as a dated decision note: what the descriptor covers, which provider-specific exceptions resisted it, and whether a staged migration is worth doing.

Not in scope: changing any launcher behaviour, migrating a second provider, or moving the launch state machine into Node. The wrappers must be byte-for-byte unchanged in what they actually execute.

Verification: the new contract tests, plus bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh and bash scripts/tests/postflight.sh proving the launchers still behave identically.
definitionOfDone: A typed provider descriptor covers argv and config construction, session mode, event capabilities, resume support, terminal handoff and failure classification
The descriptor is populated for exactly one provider and contract tests assert it reproduces that provider's current argv and config from both wrappers
A dated decision note lands in docs/plans stating what generalized cleanly, what did not, and a recommendation for or against a staged migration
No launcher behaviour changes: bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh and bash scripts/tests/postflight.sh both pass unmodified
The contract tests run in an existing suite rather than introducing a new test runner
taskRails: Spike only: the wrappers' executed behaviour must not change in this task.
One provider. Migrating a second is a follow-up decided by this task's note.
No new test runner or build tool.

implementationPlan.description: SCOPE THE SPIKE AND PICK THE PROVIDER. Read-only, no edits. This is a decision task: the deliverable is knowledge plus a small typed artifact, and the launchers must end byte-identical. (a) Establish the central constraint before designing anything: neither wrapper has a dry-run or print-argv mode. Confirm it - the only argv introspection in scripts/moe-agent.sh is the codex probe around lines 5251-5264, which appends --help to the real argv to make the CLI short-circuit, and there is no flag that prints the argv without launching. Consequence: a contract test cannot execute a wrapper to capture argv, so it must assert against the scripts as text, the way scripts/tests/parity-check.sh already extracts and compares string vocabularies across both files. That limitation is itself a finding for the decision note. (b) Choose ONE provider and record why in the step note. The recommendation is codex, because it exercises all six descriptor facets with evidence that already exists in the repository: two session modes (the interactive terminal default and the exec headless path), real config construction in .codex/config.toml including mcp_servers entries, a startup timeout, a reasoning-effort key and a tools-approval pin, sandbox argv that differs per platform, and a genuine failure classification in the argv probe that stops a seat with a named code instead of relaunch-looping. The claude provider is a worse first choice precisely because its two wrappers diverge most - one runs in the launcher directory with a temporary config, the other changes directory and merges a user-level file - and the spike should learn whether a descriptor handles the ordinary case before the hardest one. If exploration changes your mind, say so in the note and proceed. (c) Read that provider's construction sites in BOTH scripts end to end and list, literally, every argv fragment, environment key, config key and failure code it builds. (d) Confirm whether docs/plans exists and how existing notes there are named and dated. (e) Record the git status baseline for the two wrapper scripts so step 5 can prove they are untouched.
implementationPlan.note:
SCOPE + PROVIDER PICK (read-only, no edits).

(a) NO DRY-RUN CONFIRMED. `grep -niE 'dry[-_ ]?run|print[-_ ]?argv|show[-_ ]?command|noop|no-launch'` returns ZERO hits in both scripts/moe-agent.sh (6141 lines) and scripts/moe-agent.ps1 (5214 lines) = 11355 total. The only argv introspection is the codex probe (sh 5251-5264, ps1 4477-4504): it appends `--help` to the REAL argv so clap short-circuits, to detect a rejected flag. It does not print the argv. Consequence: a contract test cannot execute a wrapper to capture argv; it must assert text presence, the way parity-check.sh already does. This is a finding for the note.

(b) PROVIDER = codex, as recommended. Verified it exercises all six facets with real repository evidence: two session modes (interactive TUI default / `exec` headless via --codex-exec|-CodexExec), real config construction in .codex/config.toml, per-platform sandbox argv, a startup timeout, a reasoning-effort key, a tools-approval pin, and a genuine failure classification (MOE_CLI_ARGV_REJECTED stops the seat instead of relaunch-looping).

(c) LITERAL VOCABULARY (transcribed, both wrappers).
SHARED argv/config/env/failure: `exec`, `-C`, `--sandbox`, `-c`, `approvals_reviewer=user`, `mcp_servers.moe.env.MOE_WORKER_ID=`, `model_instructions_file=`, `--help` (probe), sandbox modes read-only|workspace-write|danger-full-access|inherit; config keys `model_instructions_file = "agent-instructions.md"`, `model_reasoning_effort`, `developer_instructions`, `project_doc_fallback_filenames`, `[mcp_servers.moe]`, `[mcp_servers.moe.env]`, `[mcp_servers.serena]`, `startup_timeout_sec`, `default_tools_approval_mode = "approve"`, `MOE_PROJECT_PATH`, `.codex/agent-instructions.md`; env MOE_CODEX_SANDBOX, MOE_CODEX_REASONING_EFFORT (default xhigh), MOE_CODEX_MCP_STARTUP_TIMEOUT_SEC (default 120), MOE_DISABLE_ARGV_PROBE, MOE_DAEMON_HOST, MOE_WORKER_ID; failure codes MOE_CLI_ARGV_REJECTED, prose `Codex command not found:`; terminal handoff `Interactive mode: polling disabled` (shared).

NINE GENUINE DIVERGENCES the descriptor must NOT flatten:
1. model_instructions_file argv VALUE: sh passes the raw temp path; ps1 passes `.Replace('\','/')` (4419).
2. Seat instructions file: sh `$(create_secure_temp)/moe-codex-instructions-${ROLE}-$$.md` (5147); ps1 `Join-Path $env:TEMP "moe-codex-instructions-$Role-$PID.md"` (4257) - not a secure temp dir.
3. sh ALWAYS emits `-c model_instructions_file=`; ps1 emits it only `if ($script:CodexSeatInstructionsFile)` (4417).
4. ps1-ONLY argv guard: `$shortPrompt -replace '"', "'"` under PS < 7.3 (4397-4399). sh has no analogue.
5. sh `rm -f "$CODEX_SEAT_INSTRUCTIONS_FILE"` after launch (5312); ps1 leaves it in TEMP.
6. `[mcp_servers.moe] command`: ps1 HARDCODES `command = "node"` (763); sh uses `$TOML_PROXY_CMD` = `$NODE_CMD` when PROXY_ARGS exist ELSE `$PROXY_CMD` alone, which emits NO `args` line at all (826-835, 878-881).
7. Post-discovery MOE_DAEMON_HOST upsert into `[mcp_servers.moe.env]`: sh ONLY (1454-1505, `DAEMON_HOST_TOML_FILE`); ps1 has only the pre-set line (752). Confirmed by grep: ps1 has exactly 2 MOE_DAEMON_HOST hits, both pre-set (codex 752, grok 1013).
8. Launch banners: sh `Starting Codex (exec, headless)...` / `Starting Codex (interactive TUI)...`; ps1 `Codex mode: exec (non-interactive, headless)` / `Codex mode: interactive TUI`. parity-check.sh does NOT pin these.
9. `developer_instructions` framing: sh emits one line (json.dumps-free triple-quoted, 950-953-ish at 858); ps1 embeds `\n` after `"""` (739). Same inner sentence, different bytes.

RESUME: codex has NO CLI-level session-resume flag in either wrapper. Resume is wrapper-level only - `claim_next_task` returns hasNext:false + alreadyAssigned and the wrapper relaunches a fresh CLI with a RESUME prompt (sh 4141-4160, MOE_RESUME_MAX_ATTEMPTS default 5). Descriptor must encode this as unsupported-at-CLI / wrapper-level.
EVENT CAPABILITIES: codex emits nothing the wrapper parses. `--output-format stream-json --include-partial-messages --verbose` + STREAM_JSON_PARSER + MOE_TOOL_WRITES_FILE are claude-ONLY (sh 5541, 5764, 5776). So codex seats cannot reach the TOOL attribution tier. Descriptor must encode `none`.

(d) docs/plans EXISTS, 7 notes, convention `YYYY-MM-DD-<kebab-slug>.md` (newest 2026-09-07-launch-checklist.md). Today is 2026-09-11.

(e) BASELINE for step 5: `git status --porcelain -- scripts/moe-agent.sh scripts/moe-agent.ps1` is EMPTY (both clean). Blob hashes: moe-agent.sh f64bdb88272f01b5904ea895211e0730c5e23716, moe-agent.ps1 f456b7d14e05c42307e6dd515863a8cdfaf367e2.

implementationPlan.description: DEFINE THE DESCRIPTOR AND POPULATE IT ONCE. Create packages/moe-daemon/src/providers/providerDescriptor.ts. It lands in the daemon package for one reason only - that is where TypeScript types and the existing vitest suite already live - and the file's header comment must say plainly that the location is PROVISIONAL, that nothing imports it, that the daemon does not and must not launch agents, and that where this belongs if the migration proceeds is one of the questions the decision note answers. Define a descriptor type with one member per facet the Definition of Done names: argv construction, config construction, session mode, event capabilities, resume support, terminal handoff and failure classification. Two design rules matter more than the field names. First, model the two wrappers explicitly rather than pretending they agree: any facet that differs between the bash and PowerShell launchers is represented as a per-wrapper value, not flattened into one - a descriptor that silently hides a divergence would be a false positive for the whole spike. Second, the descriptor is DATA describing what the wrappers do, not policy they consume: no function that builds a command line, no branching logic, nothing importable that could tempt a later change to start driving behaviour from it while the scripts still own it. Populate it for exactly the provider chosen in step 1, transcribing what the scripts actually build today - not what they ought to build. Where a facet genuinely has no answer for that provider, encode an explicit unsupported or unknown value with a comment naming the reason; leaving a field blank or inventing a plausible value would corrupt the finding. Error handling for this artifact is the type system plus the contract test: the descriptor must not be constructible with a facet omitted, so every member is required.
implementationPlan.note:
DESCRIPTOR DEFINED AND POPULATED FOR codex ONLY.

SCOPE DEVIATION (declared): the plan named one file. The first draft was 501 lines, over the 300-line quality bar, so the types and the codex data are split: providerDescriptor.ts (195 lines, types + WRAPPER_FILES + REQUIRED_FACETS) and codexDescriptor.ts (275 lines, the single populated provider). Both under 300. The provisional-location header stays in providerDescriptor.ts and names both consumers.

HEADER states plainly: location is PROVISIONAL, nothing in the daemon imports it, the daemon is state-only and must not start launching agents because a launch type sits in its tree, and where this belongs is a question for the decision note.

DATA, NOT POLICY: no function that builds a command line, no branching logic, no default-merging helper. Every export is a type or a frozen-shape const. The only runtime value besides the descriptor is WRAPPER_FILES (repo-relative script paths the test reads) and REQUIRED_FACETS (the DoD facet list the test asserts against).

ALL SEVEN DoD FACETS present and required (no optional members, so omission is a compile error): cliTypeToken, sessionMode, argv, config, events, resume, terminalHandoff, failures.

DIVERGENCE MODELLING: the core type is `WrapperFact<T> = SharedFact<T> | DivergentFact<T>`. SharedFact carries `presentInBoth`; DivergentFact carries `bash`/`powershell` values PLUS `onlyInBash`/`onlyInPowershell` exclusive literals and a mandatory `divergenceReason`. Nothing is flattened. NINE divergences are encoded as DivergentFact, not averaged away:
1. interactive banner, 2. exec banner, 3. session-mode opt-in flag spelling, 4. model_instructions_file argv value + conditional emission, 5. owned-section merge matcher form, 6. [mcp_servers.moe] proxy command (ps1 hardcodes node; sh may omit the args line entirely), 7. post-discovery MOE_DAEMON_HOST upsert (sh only), 8. seat instructions file location, 9. seat instructions cleanup, plus the PS<7.3 argv quote guard.

UNSUPPORTED MARKERS (explicit, with reasons, and deliberately carrying NO evidence literals because text presence cannot prove an absence):
- events.toolEventStream: codex emits no stream either wrapper parses; stream-json/MOE_TOOL_WRITES_FILE/the TOOL attribution tier are claude-only, so a codex seat can never reach the TOOL tier.
- events.partialMessages: no progress channel consumed.
- resume.cliSessionResume: neither wrapper passes any codex resume flag; resume is wrapper-level and provider-agnostic, so it is not a provider property at all.

EVIDENCE PRE-VERIFIED before writing: every declared literal was checked with `grep -Fc` against COMMENT-STRIPPED copies of both wrappers (`grep -vE '^[[:space:]]*#'`; ps1 has zero `<#` block comments, verified). Every `presentInBoth` literal has count >0 in both. Every `onlyInBash` has count >0 in sh and EXACTLY 0 in ps1, and vice versa. Comment stripping was necessary: raw-text `--codex-exec` and `-CodexExec` each appear in the OTHER wrapper's comments, which is exactly the false-positive trap the plan warned about.

forbiddenTokens declares `--full-auto` with its reason (0 hits in both stripped views today).

VERIFICATION: `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` from packages/moe-daemon, exit 0, no diagnostics. Line counts 195 + 275, both under the 300 cap.

Launchers untouched: no edits to scripts/. Shared-checkout dirt from other sessions left alone.

implementationPlan.description: PIN THE DESCRIPTOR TO THE SCRIPTS WITH A CONTRACT TEST. Create packages/moe-daemon/src/providers/providerDescriptor.contract.test.ts in the existing vitest suite - a task rail forbids a new test runner, and vitest is already the daemon's. The test reads scripts/moe-agent.sh and scripts/moe-agent.ps1 off disk, resolving the repository root from import.meta.url the way src/tools/registry.test.ts resolves its own directory, and fails loudly with the resolved path if either file is missing rather than passing vacuously - a contract test that silently finds nothing is worse than none. Assertions: every argv fragment, environment key, config key and failure code the descriptor declares must actually appear in the wrapper it is attributed to; a facet the descriptor marks as shared must appear in BOTH scripts; and a facet marked as diverging must appear in one and not the other, which is the assertion that stops the descriptor from quietly papering over a difference. Add the negative direction as far as it is honest: for the one vocabulary that is already enumerable, assert the descriptor declares no failure code the scripts do not contain. Be explicit in a comment about what this test can and cannot prove - it proves the descriptor's strings are present in the launchers, not that the launchers assemble them in that order, because no dry-run mode exists to ask. State that limitation here and again in the decision note rather than letting a reader assume the stronger guarantee. Keep the matching literal and anchored; a loose substring match that accidentally succeeds on a comment line would make the whole spike untrustworthy. Run npx vitest run src/providers/providerDescriptor.contract.test.ts from packages/moe-daemon and require green with nonzero counts. Sanity-check the test's own power by temporarily corrupting one declared fragment in a scratch copy and confirming it fails - restore it immediately, and never mutate the shared checkout peers are working in.
implementationPlan.note:
CONTRACT TEST LANDED IN THE EXISTING VITEST SUITE (no new runner).

File: packages/moe-daemon/src/providers/providerDescriptor.contract.test.ts. vitest.config.ts already has `include: ['src/**/*.test.ts']`, so it is collected by the normal `npm test` run, not only by an explicit path.

PATH RESOLUTION + LOUD FAILURE: repo root resolved from import.meta.url (`path.resolve(thisDir,'..','..','..','..')`), same technique as src/tools/registry.test.ts. `loadWrapper` THROWS naming the resolved absolute path and the resolved repo root if either launcher is missing, so the suite cannot pass vacuously.

MATCHING IS LITERAL AND COMMENT-STRIPPED. All assertions run against a view with full-line `#` comments removed. This was necessary, not cosmetic: moe-agent.ps1 names `--codex-exec` in a comment and moe-agent.sh names `-CodexExec` in a comment, so raw-text matching would let a divergence assertion succeed against prose. The test asserts moe-agent.ps1 contains no `<#` block comments, so full-line stripping stays sufficient. `String.includes`, never a regex, so no accidental pattern widening. Descriptor `value` prose is never asserted - only evidence literals are.

THE TEST WALKS THE DESCRIPTOR TREE rather than hand-listing assertions, so no declared fact can be skipped by forgetting to write an assertion for it. It collected 31 shared, 11 divergent, 3 unsupported facts; the suite asserts those counts are >=25, >=10 and ==3 so a walker that silently found nothing fails.

ASSERTIONS (18 tests):
- Fixtures real: both launchers >100KB raw and >1000 lines after stripping.
- Matcher power guard: a sentinel string must NOT match in either wrapper, so `contains` cannot be trivially true.
- Exactly one provider: providerId is codex AND the providers directory contains exactly ['codexDescriptor.ts'] as a populated descriptor - migrating a second would fail this.
- All eight required facet keys present (runtime mirror of the compile-time requirement).
- SHARED: every `presentInBoth` literal present in BOTH scripts; non-empty evidence; no literal shorter than 3 chars.
- DIVERGENT: every `onlyInBash` present in moe-agent.sh AND ABSENT from moe-agent.ps1, and vice versa; both evidence lists non-empty; `divergenceReason` longer than 20 chars. This is the assertion that stops the descriptor papering over a difference.
- UNSUPPORTED: reason >20 chars, and the object's key set must be exactly ['agreement','reason'] - an unsupported facet may not smuggle in evidence literals implying it was verified.
- NEGATIVE DIRECTION: MOE_[A-Z0-9_]+ vocabulary extracted from both stripped scripts (guarded as >20 codes so the subset check cannot be vacuous); every declared failure code must be in that set.
- FORBIDDEN TOKENS: `--full-auto` must appear in NEITHER launcher.

STATED LIMITATION, in the file header and repeated in the decision note: this proves the descriptor's strings are PRESENT, not that the launchers assemble them in that order or that the resulting command line matches the descriptor's prose. No dry-run/print-argv mode exists to ask. A reader must not upgrade "the strings are there" into "the command line matches".

GREEN: `npx vitest run src/providers/providerDescriptor.contract.test.ts` from packages/moe-daemon -> `Test Files 1 passed (1) / Tests 18 passed (18)`, EXIT=0.

RED PROOF - the test's own power, measured, in a SCRATCH COPY under %TEMP% (never the shared checkout). Scratch layout mirrored the repo depth (scripts/ + packages/moe-daemon/src/providers) with node_modules junctioned to the installed one. Baseline in the scratch: 18 passed, EXIT=0. Then three separate corruptions of the COPIED descriptor:
A) shared literal `approvals_reviewer=user` -> `approvals_reviewer=owner`: EXIT=1, "argv.tokensByMode.exec-headless: \"approvals_reviewer=owner\" absent from scripts/moe-agent.sh" (4 failures).
B) divergence flattened, `onlyInBash: ['TOML_PROXY_CMD']` -> `['MOE_PROJECT_PATH']` (a literal that exists in BOTH): EXIT=1, "each side-specific literal is in its own launcher and absent from the other" failed.
C) invented failure code `MOE_CLI_ARGV_REJECTED` -> `MOE_CLI_ARGV_DENIED`: EXIT=1, "descriptor declares failure codes that exist in neither launcher: expected [ 'MOE_CLI_ARGV_DENIED' ]", Tests 1 failed | 17 passed.
D) restored: EXIT=0. Scratch removed; junction deleted with (Get-Item).Delete() and the real packages/moe-daemon/node_modules/vitest verified present before and after.

LAUNCHERS UNTOUCHED: `git status --porcelain -- scripts/moe-agent.sh scripts/moe-agent.ps1` still empty; blob hashes still f64bdb88272f01b5904ea895211e0730c5e23716 and f456b7d14e05c42307e6dd515863a8cdfaf367e2, identical to the step-1 baseline.

implementationPlan.description: WRITE THE DECISION NOTE, WHICH IS THE ACTUAL DELIVERABLE. Create a dated note in docs/plans named for the provider-registry spike, following whatever naming and dating convention step 1 found there. It must answer four questions honestly, including when the answer is unflattering to the idea. What generalized cleanly: which facets transcribed into the descriptor with no loss for this provider. What resisted it: every place the two wrappers diverge, every value that is computed at runtime from the environment rather than fixed, every provider-specific exception that needed its own field or an unsupported marker, and the fact that no dry-run mode exists so a descriptor can only be pinned by text presence rather than by executing the launchers and comparing real argv. What it would cost: an honest estimate of extending this to the remaining providers given that the two scripts together run to roughly eleven thousand lines, and which of them look hardest and why - name the claude wrapper divergence and the grok constraints as the known hard cases. And a recommendation, for or against a staged migration, stated as a recommendation rather than a decision, with the smallest next step that would raise confidence - the obvious candidate being a print-argv mode in both wrappers so a future contract test could compare real command lines instead of text fragments, which is deliberately NOT done here because this task must leave the launchers untouched. Record the provider chosen and why, and note that the descriptor's location in the daemon package is provisional and load-bearing on nothing.
implementationPlan.note:
DECISION NOTE WRITTEN - the actual deliverable.

Path: docs/plans/2026-09-11-provider-registry-spike.md, following the directory's existing `YYYY-MM-DD-<kebab-slug>.md` convention (7 prior notes, newest 2026-09-07-launch-checklist.md). The filename matches the one the descriptor header already points at.

RECOMMENDATION (stated as a recommendation, not a decision; the task has no dependents):
AGAINST starting a staged migration now. FOR one narrow prerequisite first - a print-argv mode in both wrappers - then re-decide.

Four reasons, in weight order:
1. A migration cannot be VERIFIED today. With no print-argv mode there is no way to prove a registry-driven launcher builds the same command line as the one it replaced. Text presence is too weak to greenlight moving launch policy out of 11,355 lines of shell.
2. Centralizing would require picking a winner on three REAL behavioural divergences, which is a behaviour change wearing a refactor's clothes.
3. Building a registry on top of those divergences would freeze latent bugs into the specification.
4. The evidence is mixed, not negative: vocabulary generalizes very well, policy does not. A vocabulary-only registry is low-risk; an argv/config-construction registry is not, yet.

THE FOUR QUESTIONS, answered honestly including where unflattering:

WHAT GENERALIZED CLEANLY (31 shared facts): session-mode policy, the exec argv skeleton, the sandbox vocabulary (the cleanest facet - and not by accident, parity-check.sh already pins it), the config key set, and the whole failure classification.

WHAT RESISTED IT (11 divergent facts = a ~26% divergence rate on the provider chosen BECAUSE it was expected to be easy). Three are behavioural, not cosmetic, and are called out as the ones that matter: (a) the MOE_DAEMON_HOST post-discovery upsert is bash-only, so a PowerShell run that discovers the host at probe time leaves it out of the config entirely; (b) PowerShell hardcodes `command = "node"` and always emits args while bash resolves the command and may omit args entirely, so the two wrappers can emit structurally different [mcp_servers.moe] blocks; (c) the PS<7.3 quote guard MUTATES the prompt, so the two wrappers can hand codex different prompt bytes for the same task. Plus eight smaller ones.
Runtime-computed values the descriptor can name but not fix: sandbox mode, reasoning effort, MCP startup timeout, daemon host, resolved proxy command, seat instructions path, project path, worker id, prompt. Stated consequence: a registry that BUILDS argv would be a function of the environment, not a table.
Three unsupported markers with reasons: no tool event stream (stream-json / MOE_TOOL_WRITES_FILE / the TOOL attribution tier are claude-only, so a codex seat can never reach the TOOL tier - a load-bearing asymmetry a registry would expose for the first time), no partial messages, and no CLI session resume (resume is wrapper-level and provider-agnostic, so putting it in a provider registry would be a modelling error).
The decisive limitation has its own section: NO DRY-RUN MODE, checked not assumed (zero hits for dry-run/print-argv/show-command/noop/no-launch across both files). The note states plainly that a passing contract test must NOT be read as argv equality, and that parity-check.sh has the same ceiling for the same reason. The comment-stripping caveat is stated too, with the concrete reason (each wrapper names the twin's flag spelling in a comment).

WHAT IT WOULD COST: 11,355 lines total, with a measured per-provider footprint table (comment-stripped mention counts: codex 69/75, gemini 33/55, grok 72/108, claude 39/28). claude is named the hard case by STRUCTURE despite the smallest footprint - its two wrappers deliver MCP config by structurally different mechanisms (user-level merge + project .mcp.json vs a temp --mcp-config), it is the only provider running in the launcher's cwd in one wrapper, and it is the only one with an event stream. grok is named hard by accumulated exception (dotted tool names dropped, folder trust, top-level-key-free config, per-process ${VAR:-default} expansion, three auto-merge env kills, per-tool timeout overrides). Estimate: gemini ~0.75x, grok ~1.5-2x, claude ~2-3x codex, so roughly 4-6 more same-sized tasks to TRANSCRIBE all four - which buys documentation and a regression test and changes no behaviour. The migration itself is explicitly not estimated, with the reason given.

SMALLEST NEXT STEP: a print-argv mode in both wrappers, explicitly NOT done here because the headline rail forbids touching the launchers, with two follow-ups queued behind it (triage the three behavioural divergences as bugs first; then do gemini, not claude, as the second provider - cheapest way to learn whether the descriptor SHAPE survives). An "if you proceed anyway" fallback recommends going vocabulary-first and letting parity-check.sh consume the descriptor instead of its hand-maintained lists.

Provider choice and its reason are recorded, including why it

implementationPlan.description: PROVE THE LAUNCHERS DID NOT MOVE, THEN RUN THE GATES. The headline rail is that the wrappers' executed behaviour must not change, so prove it first and directly: `git diff --stat -- scripts/moe-agent.sh scripts/moe-agent.ps1` must be empty against the baseline recorded in step 1. A descriptor that required editing a launcher to make its test pass would have failed the spike, not the launcher. Then run the three gates from the repository root. The daemon suite: npm --prefix packages/moe-daemon test, Windows npm.cmd, filtering for the summary lines but capturing the exit code in a separate statement because a filtered pipeline swallows it; require exit 0 and confirm the new contract test was actually collected by the normal run rather than only by an explicit path. Then bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh and bash scripts/tests/postflight.sh, both unmodified. Run the two harnesses sequentially on an otherwise quiet box and set MOE_POSTFLIGHT_TIMEOUT_SEC=180 - the default per-wrapper sixty seconds flakes while the fleet is running its own test suites, and the heartbeat-sidecar check is the first to go. If a harness fails, capture the shortest decisive line and diagnose rather than re-running blindly, and never pipe through grep with pipefail set, which turns a failure into a silent exit code. Record every command, exit code and count for the verification argument of complete_task.

implementationPlan.note:
ADVERSARIAL REVIEW - it found two real defects in my own spike, both fixed before completion.

DEFECT 1 (the big one): presence assertions could pass on UNRELATED occurrences. Measured with a throwaway script (outside the repo): of the 65 declared literals, 22 also occur OUTSIDE every codex block (grok's parallel TOML writer, the arg parser, the attribution DENY code) - e.g. [mcp_servers.moe], [mcp_servers.moe.env], [mcp_servers.serena], MOE_WORKER_ID, MOE_PROJECT_PATH, MOE_DAEMON_HOST, config.toml, .codex, --help, startup_timeout_sec. A whole-file test would have stayed GREEN with every codex block deleted.
FIX (test-only): presence is now scoped to the codex branches, located by anchoring on each wrapper's own provider-dispatch lines (`if [ "$CLI_TYPE" = "codex" ]` / `if ($cliType -eq "codex")` up to the next gemini/grok/claude branch). Found bash 3 branches (820-989, 1462-1464, 5132-5313), ps1 4 (724-869, 3540-3546, 4244-4264, 4352-4516). Bounded: each branch <=400 lines, site view >200 lines, >=1 branch per wrapper, all asserted. Four facts whose evidence genuinely lives outside any provider branch are allowlisted by path with a reason each (TUI polling suppression x2, arg-parser opt-in flag, wrapper-level resume); allowlist entries must name real facts and its size is pinned at 4. ABSENCE for divergent facts stays whole-file (the stronger direction).
PROOF (scratch copy under %TEMP%, never the shared checkout): deleted ps1 line 762 `[mcp_servers.moe]` (codex writer) leaving grok's copy at 1037. An OLD whole-file variant of the test (generated by sed from the new one) stayed GREEN - EXIT=0, 20 passed - the regression was MISSED. The NEW site-scoped test FAILED: EXIT=1, "config.tables[0]: \"[mcp_servers.moe]\" absent from the codex branches of scripts/moe-agent.ps1". Then re-ran the three descriptor corruptions against the new test: A `approvals_reviewer=user`->`owner` EXIT=1 ("absent from the codex branches of scripts/moe-agent.sh"); B `onlyInBash: ['TOML_PROXY_CMD']`->`['MOE_PROJECT_PATH']` EXIT=1 ("config.proxyCommand: \"MOE_PROJECT_PATH\" is NOT bash-only -- it is also in scripts/moe-agent.ps1"); C `MOE_CLI_ARGV_REJECTED`->`MOE_CLI_ARGV_DENIED` EXIT=1 ("declares failure codes that exist in neither launcher"); D restored EXIT=0 20 passed. Scratch removed; junction deleted via (Get-Item).Delete(); real node_modules/vitest verified present after.

DEFECT 2: the descriptor FLATTENED two value-level divergences behind keys it marked shared.
(a) TOML value encoding: bash escapes every value via json.dumps; ps1 interpolates raw into a here-string. A quote/backslash in an operator-set MOE_CODEX_REASONING_EFFORT or MOE_DAEMON_HOST is escaped by one wrapper and written verbatim (possibly invalid TOML) by the other. Evidence: bash-only `'model_reasoning_effort = ' + json.dumps(reasoning_effort)`, ps1-only `model_reasoning_effort = "$codexReasoningEffort"`.
(b) startup-timeout validation: bash `int(os.environ.get("MOE_CODEX_MCP_STARTUP_TIMEOUT_SEC", "120"))` accepts "-5"/" 42 "; ps1 `-match '^\d+$'` rejects them -> 120.
Both added as DivergentFacts (now 13 divergent / 31 shared / 3 unsupported = 29.5% divergence, up from 11). The note gained a general lesson: a registry that pins keys but not encodings under-reports divergence.

OTHER "ought vs does" fixes: exec token `--sandbox <mode>` -> `[--sandbox <mode>]` (MOE_CODEX_SANDBOX=inherit omits it; the scripts' own comment notation); events.toolEventStream reason no longer claims codex CANNOT emit events - it says neither wrapper requests/parses one and codex's own capability is not established (avoids asserting unverified CLI facts); a comment on tokensByMode states tokens are shared at TOKEN level only, pointing at the value-level divergences.

REMAINING SCEPTIC QUESTIONS, answered:
- Comment-line matches: all matching is against full-line-comment-stripped views; ps1 has no `<#` block comments (asserted). Trailing inline comments survive - stated as a known weakness in the test header and the note.
- Does anything import the descriptor? grep across packages/ and moe-vscode/: nothing outside src/providers/. codexDescriptor.ts uses `import type` only. No child_process/spawn/exec anywhere in src/providers. tsconfig excludes *.test.ts, so only the two data/type files reach dist, as dead code. The daemon stays state-only (epic rail).
- Is the text-presence limitation in the recommendation, not buried? Yes - it IS reason #1 of the recommendation ("This is the whole argument").
- Exactly one provider: the test asserts providers/ holds exactly ['codexDescriptor.ts'] as a populated descriptor.
- Launchers byte-identical to baseline: git diff --stat empty; hashes still f64bdb88272f01b5904ea895211e0730c5e23716 / f456b7d14e05c42307e6dd515863a8cdfaf367e2.
- Project rails: no eval(/innerHTML/dangerouslySetInnerHTML/__proto__, no `any`.
- NEW in the note: parity-check.sh matches whole files, so it carries exactly the unrelated-occurrence exposure found here; added as an indepe

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: Executing the wrappers in a dry-run mode and diffing real argv - rejected because no such mode exists, and adding one would edit both launchers, which the headline task rail forbids; the note recommends it instead as the smallest next step that would raise confidence. Writing the contract test in bash beside parity-check.sh - rejected because the descriptor is required to be typed, so the test that pins it should read the same TypeScript value the descriptor exports rather than a transcription of it. Creating a new package for the registry - rejected: heavier than a spike warrants, and a task rail forbids a new build tool; the daemon package is chosen only because vitest and the type system already live there, and the header comment and the note both record that the location is provisional. Flattening wrapper differences into one value per facet - rejected as the single most damaging thing this spike could do, since the whole question is whether launch policy generalizes, and hiding a divergence would answer it falsely. Covering a second provider to strengthen the sample - rejected by a task rail; whether to do that is precisely what the note recommends or rejects.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: The decisive fact, measured on 2026-09-11: neither wrapper has a dry-run or print-argv mode. The only argv introspection anywhere is the codex probe in the bash wrapper around lines 5251-5264, which appends --help to the real argv so the CLI short-circuits before any model call - it exists to detect a rejected flag, not to expose the command line. So a contract test cannot execute a launcher and compare real argv; it can only assert that the strings the descriptor declares are present in the scripts. scripts/tests/parity-check.sh is the precedent for exactly that shape: it extracts code families, banners, settings keys and environment names from both files and fails on any asymmetry. codex is the recommended subject because the repository already documents its full contract across all six facets - two session modes, config.toml construction with mcp_servers entries and a startup timeout and a reasoning-effort key and a tools-approval pin, per-platform sandbox argv, and a real failure classification in the probe that stops a seat with a named code rather than relaunch-looping. The claude provider is the known hard case and a poor first subject: its two wrappers diverge most, one running in the launcher directory with a temporary config and the other changing directory and merging a user-level file.
planningNotes.risks: The main risk is a spike that flatters the idea. A contract test asserting loose substrings would pass against comment lines and make a shaky descriptor look proven, so matches must be literal and anchored, and the worker must verify the test actually fails when a declared fragment is corrupted - in a scratch copy, never in the shared checkout peers are working in. The second risk is scope drift: the launchers must end byte-identical, so step 5 checks that directly with a diff against the step 1 baseline rather than assuming it. Nothing may import the descriptor; the daemon stays state-only. Test-environment quirks on this box: run parity-check and postflight sequentially on a quiet machine with MOE_POSTFLIGHT_TIMEOUT_SEC=180, because the default sixty seconds flakes while the fleet runs its own suites and the heartbeat-sidecar check fails first; and never pipe a harness through grep with pipefail set, which converts a real failure into a silent exit code. Finally, the note must stay a recommendation, not a decision - this task has no dependents and exists to inform a choice someone else makes.

completionSummary:
RECOMMENDATION: AGAINST starting a staged migration of launch policy into a typed provider registry now. FOR one narrow prerequisite first: a print-argv mode in both wrappers, then re-decide. Reason #1 of 4: a migration cannot be verified today, because neither wrapper can print its real argv, so text presence is the ceiling. Full note: docs/plans/2026-09-11-provider-registry-spike.md.

EVIDENCE: codex transcribed into a typed descriptor. It has 31 shared facts, 13 divergent and 3 unsupported, so 29.5% diverge on the provider picked as the easy case. Five divergences change behaviour:
1. The MOE_DAEMON_HOST post-discovery TOML upsert exists only in bash.
2. For the moe MCP server, PowerShell hardcodes command="node", while bash resolves the command and may omit args.
3. The PowerShell 7.3-and-older quote guard rewrites prompt bytes.
4. Bash escapes TOML values with json.dumps; PowerShell interpolates them raw.
5. The two wrappers validate the startup timeout differently.
Codex has no tool event stream the wrappers parse, so a codex seat can never reach the TOOL attribution tier. Resume is wrapper-level, so it is not a provider property.

FILES: packages/moe-daemon/src/providers/providerDescriptor.ts (types, provisional location, no importer outside src/providers) and codexDescriptor.ts (codex only, pure data). providerDescriptor.contract.test.ts holds 20 vitest tests collected by the normal suite. The docs/plans note is the fourth file.

DoD CAVEAT: "reproduces current argv and config" is proven as literal presence at the codex branches of both scripts, not as argv equality. No dry-run mode exists, as the plan anticipated. Presence is site-scoped because whole-file matching missed a mutation: 22 of 65 literals also occur in grok's writer and elsewhere. The site-scoped test catches that mutation and 3 descriptor corruptions. parity-check.sh has the same whole-file exposure.
